key_insight: A single strong drive on far-detuned fixed-frequency transmons can generate a large $XX-YY$ interaction, enabling a fast $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gate with tunable $ZZ$ phase.
engineering_relevance: This provides an alternative to cross-resonance for hardware-efficient entangling gates, improving SWAP efficiency and supporting spin-model simulation on superconducting processors.
method: Apply a strong microwave drive to induce the desired $XX-YY$ coupling in the far-detuned regime.
Use a weak second tone to cancel or tune the unwanted $ZZ$ phase.
Implement and benchmark a 150-ns $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ gate and demonstrate two-spin squeezing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that $\sqrt{\mathrm{bSWAP}}$ was 33% shorter than SWAP at matched drive strengths and achieved higher IRB fidelity, while cross-resonance remained shorter for CNOT in the demonstrated setting.
watch_item: Strong-drive performance depends on multilevel transmon physics, so drive strength must be carefully optimized to avoid leakage and ensure the predicted speedups hold in hardware.
paper_title: ZZ-Free bSWAP Gates under Strong Driving in Far-Detuned Fixed-Frequency Transmons
